prompt.context: Your client, TissueCo, is a large facial tissue manufacturer that sells to retailers. While the US facial tissue market suffered operational challenges due to Covid-19, the market is forecasted to recover and grow 5.8% CAGR in 2021. While TissueCo has seen some improved numbers as they adapt to the pandemic, their profitability margin has fallen below their main competitors Kelly-Clark and Proxy and Gumbo. The CEO has invited you to help them out.
prompt.question: TissueCo's profitability margin has dropped below competitors both before and after COVID-19. How would you diagnose the root cause of this profitability gap and what would you recommend to improve it?

clarifying_info.q: Is the client focused on a specific geography?
clarifying_info.a: The client is focused on US sales only.

clarifying_info.q: What product lines does TissueCo offer?
clarifying_info.a: TissueCo produces tissues that are standard, extra soft, and tissues with lotion.

clarifying_info.q: Is there a specific profitability target the client wants to reach?
clarifying_info.a: There is no specific goal to improve profitability.

clarifying_info.q: What percentage of the population uses tissues?
clarifying_info.a: Approximately 95% of the population uses tissues, so around 300M people.

clarifying_info.q: What is the average price for a box of tissues?
clarifying_info.a: Average price for a box of tissues with 100 tissues is $5.

exhibits.title: Anti-Viral Facial Tissue Market Sizing Approach
exhibits.shows: A structured market sizing table showing the step-by-step calculation for the US anti-viral facial tissue market, with input assumptions and a final dollar market size estimate.
exhibits.data: US Population ~320M; % germ-conscious 10%; ~2 colds per year lasting 5 days; ~20 tissues/day while sick; ~50 tissues/year for other reasons; 100 tissues per box; avg price per box $5

exhibits.title: TissueCo Profit Calculations by Product Line
exhibits.shows: A table showing the profit calculations for each of TissueCo's product lines using total sales, revenue share, and profit margin, plus a row for the proposed anti-viral product line.
exhibits.data: Total sales 2020 ~$3B (rounded); Standard: 65% share, 10% margin; Super soft: 25% share, 15% margin; Lotion: 10% share, 20% margin; Anti-viral: $150M sales, $30M profit

exhibits.title: TissueCo Financial Metrics by Product Line
exhibits.shows: A reference table listing each product line's sales share percentage and profit margin percentage.
exhibits.data: Standard: 65% sales share, 10% profit margin; Super soft: 25% sales share, 15% profit margin; Lotion: 10% sales share, 20% profit margin

framework: 1. Facial Tissue Market — A. Industry (growth trends, market size, customer behavior); B. Competition (# competitors, market share, profit margin/cost structure); C. Regulatory environment
2. TissueCo — A. Revenue analysis (pricing strategy, volume dynamics, breakdown by client groups/locations); B. Cost structure (fixed: rent, SG&A; variable: labor, raw materials, utilities)
3. Financial Analysis — quantify the profitability gap vs. competitors across revenue and cost drivers

4. Growth Opportunities — A. Product differentiation (soft/lotion/anti-viral/sustainable, packaging options); B. Customer segment (at-home vs. away-from-home); C. Marketing strategy; D. Distribution strategy (supermarkets, convenience stores, online)

questions.prompt: What revenue growth ideas can you suggest to improve TissueCo's top line?
questions.guidance: Strong answers should cover: upgrading the marketing strategy (aggressive campaigns, new social media channels targeting germ-aware younger audiences); changing pricing or pricing model (maintain price but reduce volume per package, bundle with hand sanitizer, subscription model); increasing distribution efficiency (online retailers, D2C, partnerships with airlines/workspaces/schools); and expanding the value proposition (anti-viral tissues, more sustainable tissues, packaging with coupons). Key insight: given low differentiation between facial tissues, high brand awareness and active marketing are likely key drivers of sales.

questions.prompt: How big do you think the US market in dollar terms is for anti-viral facial tissues?
questions.guidance: Candidate should segment the population by germ-consciousness, estimate annual tissue usage while sick and for other reasons, convert to boxes, and multiply by price. Key insight: germ-conscious consumers have higher WTP and could improve profitability even if the segment is small.

math.setup: Start with US population, isolate the germ-conscious segment (10%), estimate tissues used per year per person, convert to boxes, multiply by average price.
steps: Annual tissue use per person: (2 colds x 5 days x 20 tissues) + 50 allergy tissues = 250 tissues/year

questions.prompt: TissueCo is considering launching anti-viral tissues forecasted to generate $150M in sales and $30M in profit. Will this increase overall profitability? (Total 2020 sales = $3.1B, round to $3B for simplicity; use Appendix 1 for revenue share and margins.)
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate dollar profit and margin for each existing product line, compute current blended margin, then compare to the anti-viral line's margin. Strong candidate notes that anti-viral's 20% margin is above the blended ~12%, so it will lift overall profitability.

math.setup: Use total sales ~$3B, apply each product's revenue share and profit margin to get segment profit; sum for total profit and blended margin; then add anti-viral and compare margins.
steps: 20% > 12%, so adding anti-viral raises overall profitability
math.answer: Current blended margin ~12%; anti-viral margin 20% — launching anti-viral tissues will improve overall profitability.

brainstorming.prompt: What revenue growth ideas can you suggest?

categories.name: Upgrade marketing strategy
ideas: Expand to new social media channels to reach and cultivate younger, germ-aware audiences

categories.name: Change pricing or pricing model
ideas: Maintain price but slightly reduce volume per package to improve margin
Bundle packages together and/or offer bundles with hand sanitizer
Introduce a subscription model (e.g., Amazon weekly)

categories.name: Increase distribution efficiency
ideas: Expand to online channels (online retailers and D2C)
Build partnerships with sectors facing rising sickness concerns: airlines, workspaces, schools

categories.name: Expand value proposition
ideas: Launch new types of tissues: anti-viral, more sustainable
Add packaging innovation: include a coupon for the next purchase

recommendation: Launch the new anti-viral tissue product line: demand for anti-viral products has increased due to the pandemic, and germ-conscious consumers' WTP is higher, yielding a forecasted 20% profit margin vs. 10% for Standard and 15% for Super Soft, which will lift the overall blended margin above the current ~12%.
Complement the launch with an upgraded marketing strategy and expanded online/partnership distribution to capture growing demand.
risks: Competitive response could force price reductions, compressing the forecasted 20% margin.
Elevated demand driven by pandemic-heightened germ sensitivity may subside over the next few years, reducing the anti-viral market size.
Supply chain clogs for anti-viral ingredient inputs could limit production capacity and increase COGS.
next_steps: Evaluate the competitive landscape and build a sensitivity analysis based on different competitive responses to the anti-viral launch.
Take a deep dive into the market model to identify the main growth drivers and determine which are most sustainable post-pandemic.
Map out TissueCo's current supply chain, identify potential weak points in anti-viral inputs, and develop contingency workarounds.
